runs.name: Distribution Solutions Group, Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$35.03** (Nasdaq close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged; the merger consideration is $35.00 cash, 8-K of 2026-07-16, 0001193125-26-306263, against a $19.31 close the day before the controller's first proposal, PREM14A 0001193125-26-377452) x **46,255,422 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover for 2026-06-30, 0000703604-26-000041; issued 47,924,087 less treasury 1,685,772 = 46,238,315 on the balance sheet) = cap **$1,620.3M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0000703604-26-000008), with the FY2022 to FY2024 10-Ks, Lawson Products' FY2021 10-K and Q1 2022 10-Q, the DEF 14A of 2026-04-01, the PREM14A of 2026-09-01 and the 2022 DEFM14A; FY2025 operating cash $83,849 thousand, D&A and capital spending cross-checked to the filed statement. Formerly Lawson Products (renamed 2022 when the controller's TestEquity and Gexpro Services were merged in for stock, a reverse acquisition); LKCM Headwater and J. Bryan King (CEO and Chairman) hold about 79% and signed on 2026-07-15 to take the company private at $35.00 cash (outside date 2026-12-31; $800M 10.000% notes due 2032 priced 2026-10-07 into escrow). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN (a holding company read by its parts; Gexpro Services decides at 52.3% of combined five-year segment operating income FY2021-FY2025, 57.3% as filed: C-parts and VMI for OEMs, about 70% of revenue under long-term agreements). **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: Gexpro's margin 4.0% in 2020 (its one year of falling volume, from the 2022 merger proxy) rising every year to 9.8% in 2025 while its own volume rose each year, not credited under the change-for-the-better convention until a full cycle; in the same years its top 20 customers rose from 63% (2020, 2022) to 75%, 82% and 83% of revenue, largest about 18%; the castle not shown open, its future not judgeable. Re-look: the first fiscal year after FY2025 in which Gexpro Services' segment revenue falls (unreadable if the take-private closes and filing stops). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: LKCM-affiliated staff paid for consulting; rent-free use of LKCM-leased headquarters space; the controller's two companies merged into Lawson for stock in 2022; discretionary 2025 bonuses to the CFO and Lawson's CEO when formula bonuses fell short; some operating-company incentive pay not borne by the company. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash before acquisitions FY2021-FY2025 average $54.6M all-equity ($26.1M equity-only; FY2025 alone $91.4M), the merger rule combining the companies for FY2021 and FY2022; about $670M of acquisition cash 2021-2025 brings the all-equity average to -$79.5M, so the literal all-spending window changes sign and gives the no-growth case alone at **-$15.12** a share; organic pair $6.62-$7.26 all-equity ($10.09-$10.39 equity-only); fair not positive all-equity (-$20.46 default, -$2.49 organic), $5.72 equity-only organic; the best case of any variant earns about 4.5% at the price. Not armed as an alert (box not OUT at Q7). Balance sheets FY2016-2026-06-30, two entities spliced (Lawson alone to 2021, the combined company from 2022): tangible equity negative or near zero every combined year; retained earnings always negative, net income 2023 to mid-2026 about $1M in sum; debt 412 to $733.8M principal, all floating; first-half 2026 receivables +$60M, operating cash $1.6M, credit-loss allowance 2.4 to 8.0; buybacks at $26-$30, above the whole computed range; material weakness at TestEquity at 2022-12-31. Competitors: the 10-K names no rival, only a peer group; the analyst took Fastenal (operating margin 19.8%-20.8% every year 2016-2025), Grainger (8.6%-15.6%) and MSC (8.0%-13.1%), margins from SEC data feeds, not read in filed statements, against DSG consolidated 2.2%-4.0%, Gexpro 4.0%-9.8%, Lawson 2.0%-6.9%, TestEquity -2.6% to 2.9%; Gexpro's own OEM-supply rivals named in no filing. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session-start git status (other companies' research folders), commit subjects (another company) and a memory index line; no blind-listed file opened. Commits one per question, 44b0daad to 4cf6bd00. Citations: the analyst's check 39 ids, 45 uses, 0 problems; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 39 ids present, 37 fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) the change-for-the-better re-look says "the business's volume or its field's volume" and the two diverge here (the field soft 2023-2025 by PMI, Gexpro's volume rising); the run took the business's own; (2) the business-of-parts threshold sits on the line and turns on whether purchase amortization from a deal between commonly controlled parties counts in operating profit; (3) no rule for a name under a signed cash take-private by its controller; (4) the merger rule does not say which side's history a reverse acquisition's statements carry, and `tools/run.py` splices the two entities' balance sheets without a marker; (5) `tools/run.py`'s D&A includes purchased-intangible amortization, so its OE D&A line is meaningless for an acquirer.
runs.narr: Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE) on Gexpro Services, the deciding part: its margin rose from 4.0% to 9.8% only in years of rising volume while its top 20 customers rose to 83% of revenue, so the change is not yet credited. The controller (about 79%) is taking the company private at $35.00 cash against a $19.31 pre-bid close; beneath the stop the owner cash after acquisitions is negative and no case earns near the floor at $35.03.
